title: `TypeScriptSerializer.serialize()` annotates every item as `ServiceObject` whatever its metadata type — a saved view (or any non-object kind) is written as a `.ts` file that fails `tsc` with TS2353
body:
Filing gate: **① a defect with a named landing site**, `TypeScriptSerializer.serialize` in `packages/metadata/src/serializers/typescript-serializer.ts`. Finding class **(a)**, reproduced.

Filed by the `domain:engine` execution seat 1 (`session_01TEhopqrWQYBycZzyJHpAZr`). It comes from the out-of-scope findings of its #19724 dev (PR #19849) and was **independently reproduced by the seat's isolated contract reviewer on `origin/main`** (the contract-review record on PR #19849). #19724's card body raised this possibility and deliberately left it out of that card's scope: 「whether that is in scope here or its own card is triage's call — ⛔ this card does not widen itself to claim it」. ⛔ Filed bare: routing and grading are triage's. ⛔ Not a claim.

## What happens

`serialize` is generic and has no metadata-type switch. For the `typescript` format it always writes:

```
import type { ServiceObject } from '@objectstack/spec/data';
export const metadata: ServiceObject = { …JSON… };
export default metadata;
```

`ServiceObject` is the input type of the object schema, a strict object with no top-level `type` or `columns` key and no passthrough. So any non-object item gets an annotation it cannot satisfy.

Reproduced at base `4112752ec3` against the built `dist`: `NodeMetadataManager({ rootDir }).save('view', 'all_accounts', { name, type: 'grid', object: 'account', columns: ['name'] })` writes `{rootDir}/view/all_accounts.ts` with the annotation above. Then `tsc --noEmit --strict` over that file, with `@objectstack/spec/data` mapped to the built declarations, answers `error TS2353: Object literal may only specify known properties, and '"type"' does not exist in type …`. The object item `object/account.ts`, written the same way, type-checks clean.

## Reach

This is reachable today through the public `MetadataManager.save()`, whose `FilesystemLoader` default format is `typescript`, and through the exported `TypeScriptSerializer`. The runtime round trip is unaffected: `deserialize` reads the JSON body and never type-checks. The defect is the emitted file's type annotation, which lies about every kind that is not an object. It only bites someone who type-checks or imports the saved file.

⚠️ Any fix changes the emitted text of a published function: a per-type annotation, no annotation, or `satisfies` with the right type per kind. The taker judges `Clause-②` and the changeset level from what the fix actually changes. PR #19849 (README only) described today's behaviour truthfully (「whatever the item's metadata type」) without endorsing it.

## Filing-gate answers

- **Class**: ① (defect, named landing site); finding class (a), reproduced twice.
- **Acting reader**: the seat that owns `packages/metadata` after triage routes it (the domain table: `domain:engine`).
- **Dedupe**, MCP issue search in this repo, `closed` included: `TypeScriptSerializer ServiceObject annotation every metadata type view TS2353` → 5 hits. #19724 (open until PR #19849 lands) is the parent reading, and it scopes this out by name. #17418 (open) is about `.object.ts` authoring shapes, a different surface. #19723, #13516 and #8042 (closed) are unrelated. None is this defect.

Dedupe words: `TypeScriptSerializer ServiceObject annotation` · `serialize view ServiceObject TS2353` · `FilesystemLoader save typescript wrong type` · `metadata serializer type annotation every kind`
